capabilities: Convert .srt/.vtt files into Markdown transcript notes via a command
Embed transcript content with transcript code blocks, inline or by file path
Open subtitle files in a read-only transcript view without conversion
Configure paragraph reflow, timestamp display, speaker formatting, and frontmatter
Make transcript text searchable and linkable as native Markdown
disambiguation: Not a speech-to-text tool; it only renders and converts existing subtitle files, it does not generate transcripts from audio.
extras: The plugin was pending Obsidian community-plugin review at the time of writing; manual installation instructions are provided. Release binaries include build provenance attestations with a verification command.
intentEvidence: Subtitles MD fills a different niche: it makes existing .srt/.vtt files comfortable to read
motivation: The README's 'Why' section says existing subtitle/transcript plugins focus on generating transcripts from audio or syncing with media, and the author wanted to fill the different niche of making existing .srt/.vtt files comfortable to read and searchable.
problem: Obsidian treats .srt/.vtt files as opaque binaries, and existing transcript plugins generate text from audio or sync playback rather than making existing subtitle files readable.
summary: Reads .srt and .vtt subtitle files as readable, searchable Markdown transcripts in Obsidian, without requiring media playback.
